category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title = 'When the child predicts the SMALLEST section — repairing the small-section trap at Grade 2'; recovery_moves = ['Visual aid with arrows.', 'Drill biggest section.', 'Spin many times to demonstrate.'] — the trap is plausible but no research citation is given, and recovery_moves are flat (not branched by what the diagnostic told you about the child).
category_feedback.required_fix: Re-anchor the trap in research-grounded probabilistic-reasoning literature for early grades — e.g., Bryant & Nunes on proportional reasoning before formal probability, or Fischbein's intuitive probability work showing children attend to absolute frequency over ratio. Then BRANCH recovery_moves: (a) if child can verbalise 'bigger section' but still picks small, do paired spin-tally so they SEE frequency match section size; (b) if child can't yet identify which section is bigger, drop back to direct visual comparison ('point to the biggest section') before reintroducing the prediction step; (c) if child says 'all sections equal regardless of size', use a 7/8 vs 1/8 extreme spinner to make the size difference impossible to miss.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Paper Spinner Set (6)' and 'Prediction Recording Mat (1 per pair)' as required prep; differentiation.for_movement_learners = 'Children physically spin a large floor spinner.' — there is no explicit no-paper, no-purchase fallback for a teacher who couldn't prep the spinner set today.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a NO-PAPER alternative to differentiation: e.g., 'No-materials version — clock-spin: child stands and points an arm like a clock hand, closes eyes, partner says STOP; predict whether arm lands in the big half (3/4 of the carpet circle marked with painter's tape or imaginary quadrants) or small quarter. Body becomes the spinner. Same prediction logic, zero prep.' This makes the lesson runnable on any day.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.activity_name = 'Lucky's Spinner Brag'; exit_routine = 'Each child writes one prediction: My spinner most likely lands ___.' — Lucky says 'bigger = more likely' inside the teacher_script but there is no distinctive quotable refrain children CHANT back, and the exit_routine is a written sentence frame, not a memorable cross-lesson chant.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Lucky a distinctive, repeatable refrain that travels through the unit — e.g., 'BIG section, BIG chance — small section, small chance!' with a hand gesture (big arms / pinch fingers). Have children chant it back at the close of minds_on, again at consolidation, and ask them to use it in Lesson 4 when predicting dice modes. Update teacher_script and consolidation.discussion_prompts so the refrain appears verbatim.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: action.steps include predicting + spinning at three stations and discussing 'equal vs unequal spinners', but children are not asked to INVENT or COMPARE prediction strategies, and expanded_walkthrough.common_misconceptions = ['Small = special.', 'All sections equal regardless of size.'] are named in plain language without grounding in named research.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a strategy-comparison move in action: after Station A, two pairs share HOW they decided which section was 'biggest' — by eye, by counting equal slices, by overlaying a finger to compare. Teacher names the strategies ('Lucky's eyeball check' vs 'slice-counting') and asks children which is more reliable when sections are close in size. In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the misconception in research terms — Fischbein's primary intuition that 'rare = more interesting / more worth predicting' or Bryant & Nunes' finding that young children attend to absolute counts before proportions.

overall_notes: Lesson 3 is solid Achieving across the board but doesn't clear the Level 4 bar in four categories. Alignment and lesson-worksheet consistency are genuinely strong (worksheet parts map cleanly to success criteria; cross-references to Day 2 are explicit). The revise is concentrated in the lesson stage — deepen the trap with research grounding and branched recovery, add a no-paper fallback, give Lucky a quotable refrain, and let children compare prediction strategies. The worksheet itself does not need changes.
